description: Irreplaceable app state on a longhorn-nobackup claim escapes every Longhorn backup — must be flagged.
input:
Review this new k3s service's storage:
```
# ansible/roles/k8s/notesdb/defaults/main.yml (a new role, not yet merged)
k8s_claims:  # noqa var-naming[no-role-prefix]
  - name: notesdb-data
    storage_class: longhorn-nobackup
    size: 5Gi

# ansible/roles/k8s/notesdb/templates/deployment.yaml.j2 (a new role, not yet merged)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: notesdb
  namespace: {{ k8s_namespace }}
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: notesdb
          image: postgres:16.3
          env:
            - name: POSTGRES_DB
              value: notes
          volumeMounts:
            - name: data
              mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql/data
      volumes:
        - name: data
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: notesdb-data
```
Context: notesdb holds the only copy of the user's notes app database. Repo convention: the Longhorn RecurringJobs back up every volume through their `default` group, and a claim on the `longhorn-nobackup` StorageClass opts out of every backup. That class is for bulky, regenerable state, and each use carries a comment saying why the data is regenerable. Everything you need is above. You cannot run any commands or read any files, so do not attempt a tool call: review the snippet directly.
rubric: PASS only if the review flags that notesdb-data holds irreplaceable, non-regenerable data on the longhorn-nobackup StorageClass, so no Longhorn backup covers it and a volume loss loses the notes, and recommends moving the claim to a backed-up class (the default `longhorn` class, or a backup tier per docs/longhorn-backup-tiering.md). Must NOT wave it through as an accepted no-backup exception: this data is not regenerable and carries no justifying comment.
